SBIR/STTR program is a Set-Aside
Small Business Innovation Small Business Technology
Research (SBIR) Program Transfer (STTR) Program
Set-aside for Small Businesses to Set-aside to facilitate cooperative R&D
engage in R&D with the goal of between business and US Research Institutes
commercialization with the goal of commercialization
Applies to federal agencies >=$100M Applies to federal agencies >=$1B in
in extramural research funding extramural research funding
3.2% = $4.1B 45% = $563M
.

Key Features of SBIR/STTR
Non-dilutive – govt. takes no equity
Small business retains Intellectual Property created
Peer-review provides Recognition, Validation, Visibility
SBIR awardees eligible for admin. Supplements, other
agency programs (e.g. I-CORPS)
Close relationship to universities:
60% awarded firms had at least 1 academic founder
30-70% projects used university equipment, consult

SBIR/STTR: 3-Phase Program
Phase 1 Phase 2 Phase 3

concept / feasibility o Prototype development, field from the laboratory
study phase testing, clinical work into the marketplace

months with up to o Generally only available to Phase funding, sales

3 years (usually 2)

SBIR vs STTR: Which one is right for you?
We ask 3 main questions to our clients:
◼
Who is the PI and where will his/her affiliation be for this work?
◼
How much of the work will be sub-contracted?
◼
Do the University-based research partners wish to be Consultants or to
work as University representatives?

Eligibility
o Only a for-profit small business can apply and be the
responsible business and technical lead
o Must have 500 or fewer employees – it doesn’t matter if
they are full-time, part time, or leased. They all count
toward the limit.
o All work must be done in the US
o Must be primarily U.S. owned, greater than 50% by US Citizens
or permanent resident aliens or owned by another small
business that is greater than 50% US owned.
o If the small business is venture backed with greater than
50% VC ownership, additional considerations come into play

Considerations – Principal Investigator
o A PI must be designated and has overall responsibility for the project. PI must be
credible in terms of education, work, and project management experience
o For SBIR the PI must be “primarily employed” by the applicant small business
o Rules for PI on the STTR are different at 4 of 5 federal agencies. NSF rule are the
same for SBIR and STTR PIs. At DOD, DHHS, DOE, and NASA primary employment can
be at either
o A single PI must usually be designated but there are exceptions at NIH where team
science is needed then it is ”multiple PIs” NSF used Co-PI on NSF STTR proposals

Prepare the Proposal
Evaluation Criteria
o Significance (commercial potential)
o Innovation
o Investigator(s)
o Approach
o Environment

Develop a Preparation Schedule
o It takes more time than you anticipate –pre-award work handled by company not OSP
o Start at the end and work backwards
o Identify resources, people and organizations you may want to include in a proposal as early as possible
o Complete company start-up and registrations once you decide you are going to apply for an award
o Allow a minimum of 10 weeks –recognizing that some solicitations do no allow for that much time
o Phase 2 applications require a Commercialization Strategy –not what most PIs are used to preparing
Review the following for developing a schedule
https://www.sbir.gov/tutorials/preparing-proposal/tutorial-2#

Budgeting Basics – Fit Project to Budget
Sample Phase I SBIR for NIH
$323,090 -Award (SBA guidance figure; NIH ICs may be higher)
$21,137- -7% profit or fee
$301,953 -Available for direct & indirect expenses
$86,272- -40% Total indirect expenses
$215,681 Total available for direct costs

SBIR/STTR Today: Shutdown challenge at NIH
Major changes:
Increased disclosure on foreign affiliations
For NIH, Institutes and Centers increase budget caps as
related to specific topics of interest (for Phase Is, several
now at $400K or $700K)
Strategic Breakthrough awards for post-Phase II awardees.
Requires VC match of funds. May be up to $30M.

SBIR/STTR Today: Changes with the Reauthorization
Other changes:
SciENcv biosketches now required
Data sharing plan for SBIRs/STTRs now Not Required (still required for
other NIH research grants)
Commercialization language strengthened – reviewers increase focus
Technical and Business Assistance (TABA) - new allowable costs
include staff training
